title: Pyrotechnic Devices: Health and Safety Precautions
introduction:
An airbag's trim cover hides a device designed to release energy on command. I treat that stored energy as the starting point for understanding every handling rule here: which way a live component faces matters, and a quiet, undeployed part still needs respect.

These precautions explain who may handle pyrotechnic components, how live devices must be carried, the conditions required for deployment, and what crash damage means for restraint mountings. They are a safety reference, not a removal, depowering or deployment procedure. Qualified personnel still need the dedicated procedures for the work being performed. I also pay attention to the mounting areas: the controller and sensors need their proper foundation, not just an undamaged-looking housing.

edits.text: WARNING: Only qualified personnel may service or handle Pyrotechnic Components. Qualification requirements vary by region; always comply with local laws and legislative directives governing this work. Failure to follow this instruction may result in serious personal injury or death.
edits.why: The qualification requirement applies to handling as well as service. Familiarity with ordinary vehicle electrical parts does not establish the required authorization or training.

edits.text: WARNING: Carry a live airbag with its deployment door, trim cover or tear seam facing away from your body. Never set it down with the deployment door, trim cover or tear seam facing down. Failure to follow these instructions may result in serious personal injury if the airbag deploys accidentally.
edits.why: The deployment face is the key orientation reference. Keep track of it both while carrying the airbag and when placing it down.

edits.text: WARNING: Before carrying or transporting a live safety belt inflator, install the safety belt buckle bolt in the inflator tube hand tight, and keep it installed during movement. Failure to follow this instruction may result in serious personal injury if the inflator deploys accidentally.
edits.why: The buckle bolt's presence is a required transport condition. Hand tight is the specified condition here; this warning does not provide a final installation torque.

edits.text: WARNING: Deploy all supplemental restraint system (SRS) devices, including air bags, pretensioners and load limiters, outdoors. Keep all personnel at least 9 meters (30 feet) away. Hearing protection is required because deployment produces a loud report. Failure to follow these instructions may result in serious personal injury.
edits.why: Outdoor location, personnel separation and hearing protection are concurrent requirements. They define safety conditions for a deployment procedure; they do not explain how to initiate deployment.

edits.text: WARNING: Never bleach or re-dye safety belt webbing; these treatments may weaken it. Failure to follow this instruction may increase the risk of serious personal injury or death in a crash.
edits.why: Appearance is not a measure of belt strength. A cosmetic treatment can compromise the webbing's restraint function.

edits.text: WARNING: After a crash, inspect the Restraints Control Module (RCM) and impact sensor mounting areas for damage or deformation. Inspect the related components for cracks, damage and loose fasteners as well. Restore any damaged mounting area to its original production configuration. After repairing a mounting area, replace the original RCM or impact sensor at that location with a new component, whether or not the airbags deployed. Failure to follow these instructions may result in serious personal injury or death in a crash.
edits.why: The mounting area and the component both matter. Repairing the mounting area does not permit reuse of the original RCM or impact sensor at that repaired location, and a lack of airbag deployment does not remove the replacement requirement.

edits.text: WARNING: After a crash in which a side airbag deployed, replace the seat backrest cover, seat backrest foam and side airbag. Inspect the side airbag mounting areas for deformation. If those areas are damaged, install a new seat backrest frame. Failure to follow these instructions may result in serious personal injury or death in a crash.
edits.why: The required replacements extend beyond the deployed airbag. The mounting-area inspection determines whether the backrest frame must also be replaced.

edits.text: WARNING: Every collision repair must include inspection and correction of all safety belt components. Use Safety Belt Inspection and Repair After a Collision in Section 501-20A, General Procedures, of this manual for the required inspection and repair instructions. Failure to follow this instruction may cause incorrect safety belt system operation and increase the risk of serious personal injury or death in a crash.
edits.why: I keep the complete belt-system check on the collision-repair list. This warning requires the named procedure; it does not provide that procedure’s inspection methods or repair decisions.

edits.text: WARNING: Whenever the Safety Canopy or side air curtain has deployed, install a new headliner and new roof pillar upper trim panels with attaching hardware. Check that the headliner carries the word AIRBAG where it meets each roof B-pillar trim panel. Remove and replace any other damaged components or hardware with new parts. Always install new torque-prevailing type J-nuts when installing the Safety Canopy. Failure to follow these instructions may cause incorrect Safety Canopy or side air curtain deployment and increase the risk of serious personal injury or death in a crash.
edits.why: The replacement requirements include the surrounding trim and hardware, not just the deployed assembly. The AIRBAG marking is a specified headliner check, and the J-nuts must be new.

edits.text: WARNING: Do not repair or service restraint-component connector terminals. When those terminals need repair, replace them using service connector pigtails. Failure to follow this instruction may cause incorrect vehicle safety-restraint operation and increase the risk of serious personal injury or death in a crash.
edits.why: A terminal is the metal contact inside the connector. The permitted repair route here is replacement with the service pigtail, rather than work on the existing terminal.

edits.text: WARNING: Never disassemble or tamper with deployable seat belt components, including pretensioners, load limiters and inflators. Never back probe the electrical connectors of deployable devices. Tampering or back probing may cause accidental deployment and result in personal injury or death.
edits.why: The connector is part of the deployment system. Back probing is expressly prohibited; it is not an acceptable workaround for accessing a measurement.

edits.text: WARNING: Never tamper with, repair or modify a Restraints Control Module (RCM) or any other Supplemental Restraint System (SRS) component. Failure to follow this instruction may cause incorrect Supplemental Restraint System (SRS) operation and increase the risk of serious personal injury or death in a crash.
edits.why: The RCM coordinates restraint deployment. Component-level repair or modification is outside the permitted work described by these precautions; use the dedicated service instructions for the required action.

edits.text: WARNING: Never probe the electrical connectors on airbag, Safety Canopy or side air curtain assemblies. Probing can cause accidental deployment, increasing the risk of serious personal injury or death.
edits.why: I treat these deployment-device connectors as a firm boundary for electrical probing. Use the dedicated restraint-system diagnostic and depowering procedures for the intended work; this warning is not a testing procedure.

edits.text: WARNING: While the restraints control module (RCM) is connected and the ignition switch is ON, do not handle it, move it or change its original horizontal mounting position. Doing so can accidentally deploy the Safety Canopy and cause serious personal injury or death.
edits.why: The restriction covers handling and changes in orientation as well as relocation. It does not establish that another ignition state alone makes module handling safe.

edits.text: WARNING: Keep objects and obstructions out of the deployment path of the Safety Canopy or side air curtain assembly. Never place any type of fastener or tie strap around any part of the Safety Canopy, side air curtain assembly or related interior trim panel. An obstruction or added restraint can make the Safety Canopy or side airbag curtain deploy incorrectly, increasing the risk of serious personal injury or death in a crash.
edits.why: I include the related trim when checking this boundary: securing trim or routing an added tie strap can interfere with the deployment path.

edits.text: WARNING: Occupant Classification System (OCS) parts are calibrated together as an assembly. Replace them only in the configuration in which they are sold, and never separate the assembly's parts. Separating them or changing that configuration can cause incorrect OCS operation, increasing the risk of serious personal injury or death in a crash.
edits.why: The calibrated assembly is the replacement unit. Treating its parts as independently interchangeable would disregard that calibration.

edits.text: WARNING: Never let oil, grease, water or foreign contaminants get on or inside occupant classification system (OCS) components or their electrical connectors. Contamination can cause incorrect OCS operation, increasing the risk of serious personal injury or death in a crash.
edits.why: I keep both the components and their connections protected from contamination during handling. This precaution does not authorize a cleaning or repair method for a contaminated assembly.

edits.text: WARNING: Always tighten the restraints control module (RCM) fasteners and the impact sensor fasteners, if equipped, to their specified torque. Incorrect tightening can cause incorrect restraint system operation, increasing the risk of personal injury or death in a crash.
edits.why: Obtain the applicable torque from the matching component procedure before fastening these parts. This safety overview gives no torque value or installation sequence.

edits.text: WARNING: When carrying a live Safety Canopy or side air curtain assembly, always keep its tear seam pointed away from your body. Accidental deployment can cause serious personal injury or death if you do not follow this instruction.
edits.why: The tear seam is where the curtain opens during deployment. I use that seam as the handling reference so the deployment opening faces away from me.

edits.text: WARNING: Never paint airbag trim covers or deployment doors. Paint can cause the airbag to deploy incorrectly, increasing the risk of serious personal injury or death in a crash.
edits.why: These covers and doors are part of the airbag's deployment path. A cosmetic change can affect how that path opens.

edits.text: WARNING: Always carry a live hood actuator by gripping around its cylinder, with the mounting bracket up and the cap pointing away from your body. When setting it down, always lay it on its side with the cap pointing away from people. Never place anything in front of the cap. Failure to follow these instructions may cause serious personal injury if the actuator deploys accidentally.
edits.why: The carrying position and resting position are different. Both keep the cap directed away from people and its path unobstructed.

edits.text: WARNING: After a pedestrian impact, inspect the impact sensor mounting areas for damage. If those areas are damaged, install a new bumper cover. Install new pedestrian impact sensors after the impact. Failure to follow these instructions may result in serious personal injury or death in a subsequent pedestrian impact.
edits.why: The bumper-cover replacement depends on damage at the sensor mounting areas. The instruction to install new pedestrian impact sensors is not conditional on finding that damage.

edits.text: WARNING: Do not repair or service the connector terminals of pedestrian protection system components. If the terminals need repair, replace them using the service connector pigtails. Failure to follow this instruction may cause incorrect pedestrian protection system operation, increasing the risk of serious personal injury or death in a pedestrian impact.
edits.why: A terminal is the metal contact inside a connector. The prescribed repair uses the service connector pigtail rather than work on the individual terminal; this warning does not supply the pigtail installation procedure.

edits.text: WARNING: Never tamper with, repair or modify a pedestrian protection system component. Doing so may cause incorrect system operation, increasing the risk of serious personal injury or death in a pedestrian impact.
edits.why: I keep the permitted service-pigtail replacement distinct from component repair. That connector instruction does not authorize opening, altering or repairing the protection component itself.

edits.text: WARNING: Never probe the electrical connectors on pedestrian protection system pyrotechnic assemblies. Probing may accidentally deploy these assemblies, increasing the risk of serious personal injury or death.
edits.why: A diagnostic probe can initiate the deployment hazard this warning is intended to prevent. Connector identification is not permission to make electrical contact with a deployment circuit.

edits.text: WARNING: Pyrotechnic components are very hot immediately after deployment and may be covered with pyrotechnic residuals. Do not handle them immediately after deployment. Always wear protective gloves, safety glasses and breathing protection to prevent skin contact with, and inhalation of, pyrotechnic residuals. Failure to follow these instructions may result in serious personal injury.
edits.why: Deployment creates both a heat hazard and a residue-exposure hazard. The required protective equipment does not cancel the prohibition on handling components immediately after deployment.
